title: sMoE: Elastic MoE-Based Inference with Serverless Computing via Fine-Grained Expert Scaling
evidence_span: sMoE models serverless MoE inference as a DAG of experts and non-MoE segments, uses a DAG neural network and layer-wise pointer network, and jointly selects vertical resources, replica counts, and concurrency per expert; the official description reports 21.4–39.2% lower serving cost than state-of-the-art solutions while meeting end-to-end P95 latency SLOs.
problem: Sparse and skewed expert popularity makes large-scale MoE inference cost-inefficient, while serverless scaling must respect cross-layer dependencies and concurrent-request SLOs.
method_or_artifact: Topology-aware serverless autoscaler using deep reinforcement learning, DAGNN cross-layer features, and layer-wise pointer decisions for expert resources and replicas.
workload_or_benchmark: Concurrent serverless MoE inference; model, request distribution, cloud platform, SLO target, cold-start policy, and cost model are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Elastic serverless resources with per-expert vertical scaling and replicas; accelerator type, memory, network, billing units, and startup latency are unspecified.
limits: The description omits model/request traces, cloud price, cold-start overhead, SLO threshold, replica churn, and baseline tuning.
Cost gains may depend on expert-skew and serverless billing granularity.
Official description only; cloud-system and quality claims require paper-level verification.

title: MoE-Balance: Unleashing the Full Potential of CPU-GPU Heterogeneity for Efficient MoE Inference
evidence_span: MoE-Balance uses a fine-grained dynamic scheduler to distribute expert tasks by real-time load and combines cross-layer prefetching with chunked PCIe transfers to overlap CPU/GPU execution and weight movement; on Mixtral-8x7B the official description reports 1.6x higher throughput and 37.5% lower end-to-end latency than hybrid baselines.
problem: MoE expert weights exceed consumer GPU capacity, while coarse CPU-GPU offloading leaves CPU resources idle and creates pipeline bubbles.
method_or_artifact: Real-time heterogeneous scheduler, expert-task balancing, cross-layer prefetching, and chunked CPU-GPU transfer over PCIe.
workload_or_benchmark: Mixtral-8x7B inference under memory-constrained hybrid CPU-GPU execution; hardware, batch/sequence lengths, memory limits, and baseline systems are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Consumer-grade GPU plus CPU memory connected by PCIe; GPU/CPU models, PCIe generation, transfer bandwidth, and memory capacities are unspecified.
limits: The description omits memory capacity, PCIe conditions, request mix, expert placement, quality, and baseline tuning.
Gains may depend on Mixtral routing and CPU/GPU balance and may not transfer to other MoE models.
Official description only; runtime and quality claims require paper-level verification.

title: GreenLLM: SLO-Aware Dynamic Frequency Scaling for Energy-Efficient LLM Serving
evidence_span: GreenLLM separates prefill and decode control, routes requests into length-based queues, fits latency-power models for prefill frequency selection, and uses a hysteretic dual-loop decode controller to maintain tail token-between-token latency; on Alibaba and Azure trace replays the official description reports up to 34% lower total energy, no throughput loss, and less than 3.5% increase in SLO violations versus default DVFS.
problem: Uniform GPU power governors ignore the distinct latency and duration behavior of LLM prefill and decode, causing head-of-line blocking and excess energy.
method_or_artifact: Length-based queueing, trace-fitted latency-power models, queueing-aware prefill DVFS optimization, and decode throughput feedback control.
workload_or_benchmark: Alibaba and Azure LLM serving trace replays; GPU models, trace sizes, SLO targets, prompt lengths, and throughput definition are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: GPU serving with controllable SM frequency/voltage and phase-specific queues; GPU generation, power measurement, governor interface, and thermal constraints are unspecified.
metrics: Less than 3.5% increase in SLO violations
limits: The description omits absolute energy, GPU/power instrumentation, SLO targets, trace replay fidelity, and controller overhead.
Energy and SLO results may depend on trace mix and frequency-state transition costs.
Official description only; serving and energy claims require paper-level verification.

title: IR-Drop Aware Global Placement with PDN Optimization and GPU-Accelerated Analysis for Mitigating Global and Local IR-Drop
evidence_span: The framework combines GPU-accelerated modified nodal analysis for IR-drop estimation, iterative power-delivery-path insertion for global robustness, and density control based on maximum tolerable load at each PDN node for local effects; the official description reports fewer IR-drop violations without additional wirelength, runtime, or routability overhead versus state-of-the-art IR-drop-aware placement.
problem: Global and local IR-drop interact with cell placement and power-delivery design, while accurate analysis can be too slow for iterative placement.
method_or_artifact: Analytical global placement with PDN optimization, GPU-accelerated MNA voltage-drop analysis, and node-specific IR-drop-aware density control.
workload_or_benchmark: Physical-design placement with power-delivery networks; designs, process node, current maps, IR-drop thresholds, and baseline tools are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Chip placement and PDN with GPU-accelerated analysis; extraction, metal layers, voltage domains, and signoff conditions are unspecified.
metrics: Significant reduction in IR-drop violations claimed
No additional wirelength, runtime, or routability overhead claimed
limits: No violation counts, voltage thresholds, design sizes, runtime, GPU, or wirelength values are supplied.
MNA accuracy and density constraints may differ from signoff power-integrity analysis.
Official description only; placement and signoff claims require paper-level verification.

title: Accshield: Operator-Aware Robust Scheduling for Fault-Tolerant AI Accelerators
evidence_span: Accshield jointly considers hardware reliability variation, operator-level error sensitivity, and inter-operator dependencies, mapping insensitive operators to faulty systolic arrays while reserving reliable arrays for critical computations; the official description reports improved reliability with minimal performance loss but gives no numeric values.
problem: Faults in multi-systolic-array accelerators propagate through dependencies and can cause more severe degradation than in single-array designs, making direct reuse of fault-tolerance mechanisms costly.
method_or_artifact: Reliability-aware scheduler using operator sensitivity and dependency information to assign work across faulty and reliable arrays.
workload_or_benchmark: Large-model operators on multi-array AI accelerators; fault models, operator set, reliability target, workloads, and performance baseline are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Multi-systolic-array accelerator with heterogeneous hardware reliability; array count, fault injection, process, and recovery mechanisms are unspecified.
baselines: single-array fault-tolerant mechanisms applied to multi-array designs
limits: No fault model, reliability metric, performance overhead, scheduling latency, or workload conditions are supplied.
Operator sensitivity may vary with data and model; mapping around faults may affect utilization and quality.
Official description only; reliability and performance claims require paper-level verification.
